## Case Converter Guide

> Source: https://816800.xyz/blog/case-converter-guide/

2026-09-01 · 5 min read
### 1. Why you need a case converter
Letter casing looks trivial, but it matters everywhere in coding, writing and data work: variables want `camelCase`, database columns want `snake_case`, paper titles want "Capitalized Major Words", SQL keywords are conventionally UPPER, and social copy often goes ALL CAPS for emphasis. Doing it by hand on hundreds of characters is slow and error-prone — a **case converter** turns those rules into one click.
### 2. Common conversion modes
- **UPPERCASE**: `hello world` → `HELLO WORLD` — good for SQL, constants, emphasis.
- **lowercase**: the clean baseline form, least error-prone.
- **Title Case**: first letter of each word capitalized — titles, nav, button labels.
- **Sentence case**: only the first word capitalized — body sentences.
- **camelCase**: first word lowercase, later words capitalized — JS/Java variables.
- **PascalCase**: every word capitalized — class and component names.
- **snake_case**: words joined by underscores — Python/Ruby vars, DB columns.
- **kebab-case**: words joined by hyphens — URLs, CSS class names.
### 3. Where each convention actually comes from
The conventions are not arbitrary — each exists because of a technical constraint somewhere in the stack:
| Convention | Used in | Why it exists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| camelCase | JavaScript, Java variables | Spaces are illegal in identifiers; capitals mark word boundaries |
| PascalCase | Class names, React components | Signals "constructable thing" — a convention many linters enforce |
| snake_case | Python, Ruby, SQL columns | Underscores survive case-insensitive collations better than capitals |
| kebab-case | URLs, CSS classes, hostnames | Hyphens are URL-safe; underscores are not word separators for search engines |
| UPPERCASE | SQL keywords, constants | Visual separation of "fixed" tokens from variable ones |
| Title Case | Headings, document titles | Editorial convention; style guides differ on minor words |
Casing conventions and the reason behind them
One detail that bites people converting to kebab-case for URLs: hyphens are word separators as far as Google is concerned, while underscores glue words together — `blue-shoes` ranks for "blue shoes", `blue_shoes` is treated as one token. That is why the kebab button, not snake, is the right choice for slugs.
### 4. Typical use cases
- **Code & variables**: turn "user order" from docs into `userOrder` / `user_order` in bulk.
- **Papers & titles**: normalize a draft title to Title Case without editing word by word.
- **CSV / data cleanup**: unify headers to snake_case before import.
- **Social copy**: ALL CAPS grabs attention (in moderation).
### 5. How to use this site's case converter
1. Open the [case converter](https://816800.xyz/tools/case-converter/).
1. Paste or type any text into the box.
1. Click the matching button (UPPER / lower / Title / Sentence / camel / Pascal / snake / kebab).
1. The result appears instantly — copy it with one click.
For multi-word identifiers, make sure the input is separated by spaces or hyphens first — "userOrder" pasted as one token has no word boundaries for the tool to detect. Convert from the raw phrase ("user order"), not from another convention's output.
### 6. Why convert locally in the browser is safer
This tool runs **entirely in your browser**. Your text is never uploaded to any server and never written remotely. Drafts, code and unpublished data stay on your own device — important when handling sensitive copy.
### Frequently asked questions
#### What's the difference between camelCase and PascalCase?
Only the first word: `camelCase` starts lowercase, `PascalCase` starts uppercase. In practice the distinction matters because many style guides and frameworks key behavior off it — React treats lowercase tags as HTML and PascalCase tags as components.
#### Which case should URLs use?
Kebab-case, all lowercase. URLs are case-sensitive after the domain, so mixed casing invites broken links; hyphens keep words distinct for both users and search engines.
#### Does Title Case capitalize "the" or "of"?
Style guides disagree: Chicago lowercases short prepositions and articles mid-title; AP capitalizes words of four letters or more. This tool's Title Case applies a common rule set — check the result against the style guide your publisher expects.
#### Can I convert a whole CSV header row?
Yes — paste the entire row. The snake_case and kebab-case conversions treat spaces and existing separators as word boundaries, so a row of mixed headers usually comes out clean. Spot-check abbreviations like "ID" or "URL" afterwards.
### Related tools
To count words and characters after editing, use the [word counter](https://816800.xyz/tools/word-counter/); for eye-catching **fancy / styled text**, see the [fancy text generator](https://816800.xyz/tools/font-changer/); more notes in the [blog](https://816800.xyz/blog/).

## Word Counter Guide

> Source: https://816800.xyz/blog/word-counter-guide/

2026-09-01 · 5 min read
### 1. What a word counter tells you
Many think word counting is just "how many words" — but it also gives **word count, character count (with/without spaces), paragraphs and sentences**, plus the two that matter most: **reading time** and **keyword density**. Those numbers help with essays, SEO copy and social posts alike.
### 2. How words and characters are counted
- **Words**: the number of space/punctuation-delimited tokens — the metric English writing cares about most.
- **Characters**: counted per character, usually split into "with spaces" and "without"; handy when a tweet or résumé has a hard limit.
- **Paragraphs / sentences**: a quick read on whether structure is too bloated or too fragmented.
### 3. Keyword density & SEO
Keyword density = (keyword occurrences) ÷ (total words). It's a classic SEO signal: too low can look "off-topic", too high looks like stuffing (which search engines penalize). Keeping a primary term around **1%–2%** reads naturally; relevance and fluency matter more than the exact number.
### 4. Estimating reading time
Rule of thumb: adults read about **200–250 words per minute**. Divide total words by 220 to estimate minutes. This site shows "X min read" directly, so you can label posts and set reader expectations.
The 220 wpm figure is a midpoint, not a law. Skimmers move faster, dense technical text slows readers down, and non-native audiences often read 30–40% slower. When precision matters — course material, legal copy, subtitles — time a real reader once and calibrate your own divisor.
### 5. Limits you should know before you rely on one
Every platform counts differently, and the differences are big enough to cause rejected submissions. The table lists the cases people hit most often:
| Context | Typical rule | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| University essays | Words, excluding citations and sometimes headings | Footnotes may or may not count — check the handbook |
| News / magazine pitches | Words including headlines | Editors usually expect within ±10% of the ask |
| Social posts (X, LinkedIn) | Characters, not words | Links and emoji count toward the limit |
| Meta descriptions | ~155 characters before truncation | Titles truncate around 60 characters |
| Ad copy | Characters per line | Leading/trailing spaces can still count |
Where counting rules diverge
Practical takeaway: use the live counter while drafting, then verify against the target platform's own counter before submitting. Where the two disagree, the platform wins.
### 6. How to use this site's word counter
1. Open the [word counter](https://816800.xyz/tools/word-counter/).
1. Paste or type text; stats update live.
1. Check word count, characters, reading time and keyword density.
1. To normalize casing, use the [case converter](https://816800.xyz/tools/case-converter/) alongside it.
### 7. Privacy note
This counter runs **entirely in your browser**; text is never uploaded. Unpublished drafts and client documents are safe to paste.
### Frequently asked questions
#### What counts as a "word"?
Any run of characters separated by spaces or punctuation. "State-of-the-art" is one word; "2026" is one word. Different tools may disagree by a few percent on hyphenated or numeric text — again, the receiving platform's counter is the authority.
#### Is keyword density still an SEO ranking factor?
Not directly. Modern search engines judge topic coverage and quality, not keyword ratios. Density is still useful as a *sanity check*: if a term crosses roughly 3% the page usually reads as stuffed, and if your target phrase never appears the page may struggle to rank for it.
#### How long should a blog post be?
Long enough to cover the topic and no longer. As anchors: a focused how-to lands around 800–1,200 words, a comparison piece 1,200–2,000. Reading time is the better label for readers; word count is the better budget for you.
#### Does the counter work with languages other than English?
Character and paragraph counts work for any text. Word counting is most accurate for space-delimited languages such as English; for unspaced scripts the character count is the meaningful number.
### Related tools
To normalize titles or variables to one casing, use the [case converter](https://816800.xyz/tools/case-converter/); for eye-catching **fancy / styled text**, see the [fancy text generator](https://816800.xyz/tools/font-changer/); more notes in the [blog](https://816800.xyz/blog/).

## Fancy Text Guide

> Source: https://816800.xyz/blog/fancy-text-guide/

2026-09-01 · 5 min read
### 1. What "fancy text" is
"Fancy text" isn't a different font file — it maps each ordinary letter to **another glyph in Unicode**. For example `A` becomes mathematical bold `𝐀`, Fraktur `𝔄`, or circled `Ⓐ`. Because these are standard Unicode code points, they display anywhere that supports them — no font install needed on the reader's side.
### 2. Why it shows up on social
Instagram, Twitter/X, TikTok, WeChat and others render the Unicode basic and many supplementary planes. The styled text this site produces is just a "legal character sequence", so it displays normally in bios, display names and comments. Note: text baked into an image (e.g. an avatar) won't change — that's pixels, not characters.
### 3. Common styles
- **Bold / Italic**: mathematical alphanumeric symbols (𝐀𝐚, 𝐴𝑎) — the most universal emphasis.
- **Script / Cursive**: 𝒜𝒶 and similar — great for names and signatures.
- **Small caps / Fullwidth**: light decoration or alignment.
- **Circled / Squared**: Ⓐ ⓐ — username accents.
- **Spaced text**: inserting space characters between letters for a "wide" look.
Each family lives in a different Unicode block, and that determines where it will and won't render:
| Family | Unicode block | Code points | Reliability on social platforms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Math bold / italic | Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols | U+1D400–U+1D7FF | Highest — renders on all major apps |
| Script / Fraktur | Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols | U+1D400–U+1D7FF | High, but some fonts lack double-struck glyphs |
| Circled / squared | Enclosed Alphanumerics | U+2460–U+24FF and U+1F130– | Good for single letters, weaker for long runs |
| Fullwidth | Halfwidth and Fullwidth Forms | U+FF01–U+FF5E | Excellent (designed for CJK text) |
| Zalgo / combining marks | Combining Diacritical Marks | U+0300–U+036F | Unpredictable — can break layouts and screen readers |
Style families and where they render reliably
### 4. Use cases
- **Social bio / display name**: stand out in the feed.
- **Post titles**: bold or script to grab attention.
- **Game ID / signature**: personalize your tag.
- **Chat / comment accent**: lightweight decoration.
### 5. How to use this site's fancy text generator
1. Open the [fancy text generator](https://816800.xyz/tools/font-changer/).
1. Type or paste plain text.
1. Each style previews live; one click copies it.
1. Paste the result wherever you want.
The conversion is a fixed character map — the same input always produces the same output, on your device, with nothing uploaded. That also means it works offline once the page has loaded.
### 6. Caveats
Some older systems or fonts don't render certain supplementary-plane characters and show a box. Search engines generally **don't index** decorative glyphs, so don't use them on keywords you need to rank for. Also, always use plain text for passwords and verification codes to avoid copy errors.
Three more boundaries worth respecting. Accessibility: screen readers may spell styled characters out letter-by-letter or skip them, so never set essential information (prices, dates, warnings) in fancy text. Findability: users cannot type styled glyphs into a search box, so keep your searchable name in plain text and use the styled version as a display decoration. Stability: platforms periodically tighten username rules — a styled name that passes today may be reset to plain text after an update, so don't build your identity on it.
### Frequently asked questions
#### Is fancy text a font?
No. A font changes how glyphs look; fancy text swaps in different characters entirely. That's why it survives copy-paste between apps without installing anything — and why search engines treat it as gibberish.
#### Why does my styled text show boxes on some devices?
The device's system font lacks glyphs for those supplementary-plane code points. There is no sender-side fix; choose a more conservative style (bold, fullwidth) for audiences on older devices.
#### Can fancy text be used for passwords?
Absolutely not. Password fields expect exact plain characters, and a styled 𝐀 is a different code point from A. Use styled text only where the characters are display-only.
#### Does it affect character limits?
Yes — most platforms count Unicode code points (or even UTF-16 code units), so a styled letter can cost more than one "character". Check your final text with the [word counter](https://816800.xyz/tools/word-counter/) before posting close to a limit.
### Related tools
To count words/characters of your copy, use the [word counter](https://816800.xyz/tools/word-counter/); to normalize a title to one casing, see the [case converter](https://816800.xyz/tools/case-converter/); more notes in the [blog](https://816800.xyz/blog/).

## About 816800.xyz

> Source: https://816800.xyz/about/

Last updated: 2026
816800.xyz is a **pure front-end, ad-free** minimal tech toolkit. We gather the scattered small tools developers use daily into one unified, restrained, high-quality dark interface — "open, use, done."
### Why we exist
When debugging streams, parsing JSON or compressing images, developers often jump between sites full of popups and tracking scripts. We believe a tool should be like a Swiss Army knife — sharp, reliable, unobtrusive. This site runs no auto-ads and injects no tracking pixels; every core feature runs locally in your browser.
### How our tools are built
Every tool here follows the same three rules, which explain most of our design decisions:
- **No build step, no framework.** Hand-written HTML, one hand-tuned CSS file and vanilla JavaScript. There is no bundler to break and no large runtime to download before the tool becomes usable.
- **Vendor libraries are served locally.** `hls.js`, `dash.js` and `Plyr` live in `/assets/vendor/` on our own domain, so no third-party CDN can inject code into your session or log your address.
- **Computation happens on your device.** Text conversion, word counting, font mapping and stream decoding all run inside the browser tab. Your input is never uploaded anywhere to be processed.
### Tech stack
- **Static hosting**: Cloudflare Pages global CDN — zero server cost, high concurrency, and naturally resistant to defacement.
- **Front-end**: pure static HTML5 + a hand-crafted dark-theme CSS, zero redundant bundling, Core Web Vitals by default.
- **Player core**: hls.js decodes M3U8/HLS, dash.js decodes MPD/DASH, and Plyr provides a flat playback UI.
### What "privacy-first" actually means here
Lots of sites claim it, so here is the concrete version — what this site does, and what it never does:
| What happens | What never happens |
| --- | --- |
| Recent stream URLs and tool preferences are kept in your browser's localStorage, on your device only. | We run no user accounts, and there is nothing to sign up for. |
| The M3U8 player and text tools process what you paste locally, inside the tab. | Your URLs, text or files are not uploaded to, or stored on, our servers. |
| We measure aggregate page views with Google Analytics 4 to see which tools are worth improving. | We do not sell, rent or trade personal data, and we run no cross-site advertising trackers. |
How data is handled on 816800.xyz ``[](https://816800.xyz/m3u8-player/)
You can wipe everything the site has saved by clearing site data in your browser. The full legal version lives in our [privacy policy](https://816800.xyz/privacy/).
### Who these tools are for
- **Streaming engineers and QA testers** who need to confirm that an HLS or DASH manifest actually plays before shipping it.
- **Developers** who want a fast case converter or word counter without hitting a signup wall.
- **Writers, students and marketers** checking reading time, keyword density and platform character limits.
- **Anyone on a locked-down machine** where installing software is not an option — a browser is all you need.
### How we decide what to build next
A tool only gets added if it passes three tests: it solves a recurring problem we have personally hit, it can run entirely client-side, and it is meaningfully better than the ten results already ranking on page one. That last test is why the site grows slowly — roughly one new tool every one to two months rather than a batch of thin clones.
### Tool roadmap
We follow a "framework first, features unlocked in batches" strategy. The [M3U8 / HLS online player](https://816800.xyz/m3u8-player/) is already live; a new tool from the placeholder cards (e.g. local WebP compression, JSON conversion, QR generation) unlocks every 1–2 months to keep the site fresh.
### Frequently asked questions
#### Is everything really free?
Yes. Every tool is free, with no usage cap, no watermark and no account. We keep the whole toolkit open instead of putting features behind a login.
#### Do I need to install anything?
No. If your browser can load this page, it can run every tool on it. An up-to-date Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari gives the best results, especially for HLS and DASH playback.
#### Can I use the output commercially?
Yes. Converted text, generated short links and counting statistics are yours to use, including in commercial work. We claim no rights over what you process.
#### Something is broken — who do I tell?
Use the [contact page](https://816800.xyz/contact/) and include the tool name, the input you used and your browser. A concrete bug report is the fastest way to get a fix prioritised.
### Who writes this site
**Wen Lau** builds and maintains 816800.xyz — the tools, the player and the documentation. That is a pen name, chosen so there is a specific person accountable for what this site says rather than an anonymous template, while keeping my personal details off the internet.
What that name is actually responsible for:
| Area | What it means concretely |
| --- | --- |
| Streaming tools | Maintains the M3U8/HLS and MPD/DASH player, its CORS diagnostics and the test source list. Public test streams are re-checked periodically and replaced when they stop responding |
| Written documentation | Writes and revises every guide here. Wherever a guide quotes a number — latency, bitrate, response time, error codes — it came from a request run against a real endpoint, not from summarising a specification |
| Text tooling | Implements the case converter, word counter and fancy text generator so they run entirely client-side, with no network call |
| Corrections | Owns factual errors in this content. If something here is wrong, report it and the page gets fixed with an updated revision date |
Working areas beyond this site: HTTP adaptive streaming (HLS, LL-HLS, MPEG-DASH), browser media APIs including Media Source Extensions, and front-end tooling that runs without a backend. Every measurement published on 816800.xyz is dated and describes the conditions it was taken under, because a number without conditions is not evidence.
### Contact us
Any suggestions or want to request priority for a tool? Reach us via the [contact page](https://816800.xyz/contact/).

## Contact

> Source: https://816800.xyz/contact/

We value every message
Have a tool idea, hit an error, or want to request priority for a feature? Fill in the form below and it will open in your email client to reach us (this is a pure static site, so the form never passes through a server — privacy guaranteed).
### What we can help with
- **Bug reports** — a tool returned the wrong result, froze, or failed to load a stream.
- **Stream debugging** — an M3U8 or MPD URL refuses to play and you want a second opinion on whether the manifest, the codec or CORS is at fault.
- **Feature requests** — a tool you wish existed, or an option missing from one that does.
- **Content corrections** — something in a guide is out of date, inaccurate or missing a step.
- **Link exchange and partnerships** — see the criteria on our [friends page](https://816800.xyz/links/).
### What to include so we can actually help
The single biggest cause of a slow fix is a report we cannot reproduce. Copy this checklist into your message:
1. Which tool or page, with the full URL if you have it.
1. The exact input — the stream address, the pasted text, or the file type.
1. What you expected, and what actually happened.
1. Your browser and operating system, for example "Firefox 141 on Windows 11".
1. Any error text from the page or the browser console.
For stream problems, the [M3U8 player](https://816800.xyz/m3u8-player/) prints a built-in diagnostic that separates "URL unreachable" from "blocked by CORS". Pasting that line into your message saves a full round trip.
### Response times
| Type of message | What to expect |
| --- | --- |
| Bug report that breaks a tool | Investigated within 2–3 business days |
| Feature request | Acknowledged and added to the roadmap; shipped only if it clears our three-test bar |
| Content correction | Fixed or answered within a week |
| Link exchange | Reviewed within 1–2 weeks |
| Anything commercial | Answered as time allows — we do not sell placements |
Typical reply windows — we are a small team, so treat these as targets, not guarantees
### Frequently asked questions
#### Where does my message go?
Nowhere until you send it. This is a static site with no back end, so the form only assembles a draft inside your own email client, addressed to **admin@816800.xyz**. Nothing is written to a database, and we never see your address until you choose to send.
#### Do you offer paid support or custom tools?
Not at the moment. The toolkit is free and support is best-effort. If you need contractual response times, we are the wrong contact.
#### Can you help me play a stream that isn't mine?
We can explain why a stream fails at a technical level — CORS headers, unsupported codecs, expired tokens, geo-blocking — but we will not help circumvent access controls or DRM on content you do not own.
#### Do you accept guest posts or paid links?
No. Every guide on this site is written by us and we do not sell links. Genuine link swaps with sites we actually use are welcome; details are on the [friends page](https://816800.xyz/links/).

## Friends & Links

> Source: https://816800.xyz/links/

Recommended
Sites and partners we trust and recommend. We link to each other to grow together.
HandyTools handytools.eu.cc Free browser-based tools that run fully on your device — private by design, no signup, no tracking. MetaAI metaai.indevs.in A directory of 788+ AI tools across 35 categories — image, writing, coding, video, audio and chatbots, with bilingual guides.
### How we choose the sites listed here
A link from us is a recommendation, so the bar is higher than "you linked to us first". Every site above was checked against the same four questions:
- **Does it actually work?** We open it and use the main feature. Broken flows, dead links or a wall of popups disqualify a site immediately.
- **Is it useful to the same reader?** Our audience is developers, streaming engineers and technical writers. A well-made tool or a genuine directory fits; unrelated content does not.
- **Does it respect the visitor?** No forced signup just to try the feature, no aggressive ad layouts, and ideally work that stays on the device.
- **Is it maintained?** Something touched in the last few months, not a project abandoned years ago.
### Want to be added?
Send the site URL and one line on what it does via the [contact page](https://816800.xyz/contact/). We review requests within one to two weeks and reply either way — a silent no is not how we work.
We do not require a reciprocal link and we do not accept payment for placement. If your site is a good fit we will list it whether or not you link back; if it isn't, no amount of link swapping changes that.
### Frequently asked questions
#### Do I have to link back to 816800.xyz?
No. A reciprocal link is welcome but never a condition. We would rather list a genuinely useful site than trade favours.
#### My site is listed but has changed since then.
Tell us and we will update or remove the entry. Listings are reviewed periodically, but we would rather hear it from you first.
#### Do you list competitors?
Yes, if they are good. A reader who needs a working tool matters more to us than defending a keyword.
#### Why are there only two sites here?
Because we would rather have two links we stand behind than twenty that pad the page. The list grows when we find something worth recommending, not on a schedule.
Want to swap links? [Get in touch](https://816800.xyz/contact/).
